summary: AI observability matters because LLM applications introduce unique failure modes—hallucinations, prompt drift, latency spikes, and runaway token costs—that traditional APM tools cannot detect. As the LLM observability platform market grows from $2.69 billion in 2026 toward $9.26 billion by 2030 at a 36.2% CAGR, teams need dedicated tooling to trace every prompt and completion, evaluate output quality, and attribute spend to specific users or features. Gartner predicts LLM observability investments will account for 50% of GenAI deployments by 2028, up from 15% in early 2026, making early adoption a competitive advantage.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, chain steps, agent runs, prompt versions, evaluation scores, and token usage across LangChain and non-LangChain applications
features: End-to-end trace visualization for chains and agents
Built-in prompt hub for versioning and A/B testing
Human and automated evaluation workflows
Dataset management for regression testing
LangChain-native deep integration with span-level detail
Feedback collection and annotation tools
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39/seat/month with overage at $2.50 per 1,000 traces at standard retention; approximately $264 for 100,000 traces on Plus; Enterprise pricing available with custom retention and SSO
tools.best_for: Teams already using LangChain or LangGraph who need deep chain-level tracing, prompt versioning, and structured evaluation pipelines in a single integrated platform

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests, token consumption, latency, cost per request, user-level spend, and model performance across 300+ supported models
features: Single base-URL proxy integration requiring one line of code change
Cost visibility and attribution by user, department, or feature
Support for 300+ models via open model-cost repository
Prompt caching and rate limiting controls
Open-source and fully self-hostable
SOC-2 Type II and HIPAA compliance on Team tier
Real-time cost alerts and budget guardrails
tools.pricing: Hobby tier free at 10,000 requests/month; Pro at $79/month with unlimited seats and usage-based costs beyond included volume; Team at $799/month adding SOC-2 Type II and HIPAA; custom Enterprise pricing with SAML SSO and on-premises deployment
tools.best_for: Teams needing instant cost governance and spend visibility in under five minutes, especially those monitoring multi-model environments or enforcing departmental budget limits without deep framework dependencies

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B) Weave
tools.monitors: LLM experiments, prompt evaluations, model fine-tuning runs, artifact lineage, inference traces, and production monitoring for generative AI applications
features: Experiment tracking with full artifact versioning
Weave tracing for production LLM calls and agent flows
Integrated evaluation framework for comparing prompt and model versions
Dataset and model artifact registry
Collaboration dashboards for ML and LLM teams
Native integrations with major LLM providers and frameworks
tools.pricing: Free tier available for individuals; Team plans start at $50/month per seat; Enterprise pricing on request; W&B Weave usage may be metered separately from core W&B platform depending on plan
tools.best_for: ML and research teams that already use W&B for experiment tracking and want to extend the same workflow to LLM prompt engineering, fine-tuning evaluation, and production tracing within one unified platform

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: LLM traces, retrieval quality for RAG pipelines, embedding drift, model performance degradation, hallucination signals, and prompt-response quality at scale
features: Long-standing ML monitoring extended to LLM and RAG use cases
Arize Phoenix open-source local observability companion
Retrieval relevance and context quality scoring for RAG
Embedding visualization and drift detection
Integration with OpenTelemetry-compatible instrumentation
Online evaluations with LLM-as-judge scoring
Custom dashboards and alerting
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is fully open-source and free to self-host; Arize managed cloud platform offers a free Developer tier with limited volume; Team and Enterprise tiers are usage-based with custom pricing; contact sales for production-scale quotes
tools.best_for: Enterprise teams running RAG pipelines or complex multi-step LLM applications who need production-grade retrieval quality monitoring, embedding drift detection, and evaluation at scale with strong ML observability heritage

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, spans, prompt versions, evaluation scores, token costs, user sessions, and feedback signals across any framework or language
features: Framework-agnostic tracing via OpenTelemetry or native SDKs
Prompt management with versioning and rollback
Online and offline evaluation pipelines
Cost tracking broken down by model, user, and session
Open-source and fully self-hostable on your own infrastructure
Human annotation queues and feedback collection
Native integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and raw API calls
tools.pricing: Open-source self-hosted version is completely free; Langfuse Cloud Hobby tier is free with limited volume; Pro tier at $59/month includes higher limits; Team and Enterprise tiers available with custom pricing, SSO, and SLA support
tools.best_for: Teams that want a fully open-source, self-hostable observability stack with strong prompt management and evaluation capabilities, especially those with data residency requirements or preference for avoiding vendor lock-in

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM API calls, token usage, latency, and model interactions via OpenTelemetry-standard instrumentation compatible with any existing observability backend
features: OpenTelemetry-native SDK requiring minimal code changes
Automatic instrumentation for OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, and other providers
Exports traces to any OTel-compatible backend such as Datadog, Grafana, Jaeger, or Honeycomb
Vendor-neutral design preventing observability lock-in
Lightweight and low-overhead for high-throughput production use
Community-maintained provider support via open-source contributions
tools.pricing: Fully open-source and free; costs are determined entirely by the observability backend you choose to export data into; no proprietary SaaS fees from the OpenLLMetry project itself
tools.best_for: Engineering teams with an existing OpenTelemetry-compatible observability stack who want to add LLM-specific instrumentation without adopting a new SaaS platform, keeping all data within their current infrastructure

cost_tips: Implement prompt caching aggressively: tools like Helicone expose cache hit rates across 300+ models, and enabling semantic or exact-match caching on repeated or near-identical prompts can reduce token spend by 40-70% on high-volume applications without degrading response quality

Set per-user and per-feature budget guardrails before you scale: use observability tools to attribute cost by user ID, team, or product feature from day one, then configure hard limits and alerts so a single misbehaving agent or a spike in user traffic cannot generate unbounded API spend

Right-size your model selection with trace data: use evaluation frameworks like Langfuse or LangSmith to benchmark smaller, cheaper models against your actual production prompts and quality thresholds—many tasks that teams default to GPT-4-class models can be handled at a fraction of the cost by smaller models with minimal quality loss

Audit and compress prompt templates regularly: long system prompts with redundant instructions are one of the largest hidden cost drivers; use prompt versioning in LangSmith or Langfuse to A/B test trimmed prompt variants, and monitor token counts per trace to catch prompt bloat before it compounds across millions of requests
